representation_paths.memory_component: reusable explicit rules and strategies abstracted from execution experience and hypothesis evidence

evidence.paraphrase: The Slow System abstracts recurring M1 execution records and M2 hypothesis evidence into M3 reusable cognition, depicted as rules and strategies. M3 is retrieved alongside M2 for subsequent experiments. A frozen LLM operator updates the retrieval index or M3 according to a selected memory action while preserving raw M1 records and M2 evidence updates.

A trainable Manager scores memory-action/target candidates using current experience and retrieved records. Its action space contains Retain, Merge, Abstract, Compress, Forget, and Skip. PPO trains the selection policy using subsequent task improvement, uncertainty reduction, and experiment cost. This supports learned memory-operation selection, but does not by itself establish deployment-time policy updates.

The frozen Qwen3.5-122B-A10B operator executes the Manager-selected action and target to update the retrieval index or M3. Memory contents can therefore change without requiring an update to the operator model.

Merge is an explicit candidate memory operation applied to selected target records or evidence groups. The main text supports merging; it does not separately establish a particular deduplication algorithm.

Across episodes, recurring execution experience in M1 and hypothesis evidence in M2 are abstracted into reusable M3 cognition. The hierarchy preserves experience for later adaptation rather than only the current task context.

Matched physical trials update hypothesis support/refutation counts and posterior confidence. Positive measured code-skill joint gain supports works-with relations, while revision edges retain hypothesis history. These updates change stored evidence and beliefs; posterior changes alone are not counted as memory-management-policy evolution.

The Manager retrieves across M1-M3, and M2/M3 guide later experiments, combining native source evidence and explicit abstractions in one operative memory hierarchy.

adjudication_notes: Re-adjudicated on 2026-10-16 following author clarification supplied by the user. The two clarifications are recorded as author correspondence, distinct from published-paper evidence; no independently obtained correspondence transcript or public URL is claimed.

T3 supersedes the provisional T2 assignment because the authors confirmed that PPO updates the Memory Manager policy during continuous interactive learning. An MLP/softmax action selector alone would not establish T3.

Maintenance-policy evolution is supported by feedback-driven changes to the policy selecting retention, merging, abstraction, compression and forgetting. No separate retrieval-policy evolution or Architect-based instruction evolution is asserted without further evidence.

Hybrid is now supported by native M1 execution trajectories together with M2 structured hypotheses and M3 abstract rules/strategies. Source-preserving/modality-native and cross-represented explicit parent families are both counted. The exclusive representation matrix counts this architecture once in Hybrid, not once in each exclusive row.
Native M1 retention does not establish that raw RGB, depth images or every possible sensor stream is preserved. No such unsupported modality or file-format claims are added.
The Manager MLP is a memory-management policy, not an additional latent/parametric memory representation. Its trainability is therefore not counted as a separate Axis I family.

The Architect instruction-refinement mechanism remains unspecified; T3 does not rely on this candidate route. The v1 PDF references appendices not included in the reviewed 12-page PDF, so implementation details beyond the author clarifications remain unverified.
Included as one embodied architecture/method. Evaluation on existing benchmark environments does not create a new benchmark record.
